title: Red-cell size variability adds no established hearing-discrimination gain beyond mean cell measures across two NHANES samples
abstract: We tested whether red-cell distribution width (RDW) adds hearing-impairment prediction beyond hemoglobin, mean cell volume, white-cell count and conventional risk factors. Models fitted in NHANES2015–16 (n=2405;317 events) were frozen and tested in separately sampled NHANES2003–04 (n=878;126 events). Weighted AUC changed from 0.709005 to 0.708730; delta -0.000276, conditional95% PSU-bootstrap interval [-0.001771,0.001319]. Log loss decreased by 0.000992, but its interval included zero improvement. Source-refit uncertainty and sensitivity analyses did not establish discrimination superiority. This negative result concerns one linear RDW representation and independently sampled cycles of the same survey, not independent-study clinical validation or absence of physiological information.

citations.reason: Primary RDW/hearing association study motivates distinct incremental prediction test; no estimates or individual data reused.
Public confirmation audiometry data and special subsample weights.
